Not necessarily. The two sources answer different questions, so they are consistent here.

Hansen records when tree cover (≥30% canopy in 2000) was lost. It shows 67.7 ha lost in 2020, plus earlier losses in 2008, 2015 and 2017. JRC GFC2020 is a forest/non-forest map for the end of 2020. It shows 0 ha of forest on the asset.

If the 2020 clearing happened before JRC's reference date, JRC would correctly show no forest afterward. This also explains why the 2020 event is history and not a post-baseline loss.

One caution: Hansen's 2000 tree cover is only 23 ha, yet it reports 67.7 ha lost in 2020. That mismatch could reflect regrowth or plantation cycles, and the tool doesn't resolve it. Check it if the 2020 figure matters.

For the claim period (2021–2025), no loss event of 0.5 ha or more was detected. Only 0.4 ha of sub-threshold loss appeared in 2021. This is not a compliance finding.
